title: Continuous span and shape across torque budgets 0.5-2 N·m, 0.5 mm FAAV sheet
author: sam
question: For the FAAV sheet (0.5 mm, pivoting on a stiff leading edge) at 1 Hz, with half-span free, how do the best thrust, half-span and outline change with peak-torque budget from 0.5 to 2 N·m, and where does the 400 mm single-sheet limit start to cost thrust?
notes: Boundary condition: the FAAV build. A 0.5 mm carbon sheet on a stiff leading edge that the sheet pivots about; the leading edge itself neither bends nor twists. That is the chordwise t0.50 model: the leading edge is held straight and in place, each strip pitches about it against the sheet's own torsion and warping, root fixed to the hub; the rod is not modelled (its torsion excluded, its mass on the pitch axis). Companion to 2026-11-25-free-span-1nm, which covers 1 N·m with finer steps. Twelve lineages per budget (3 families x 4 half-spans), span a search coordinate (20 mm step, 10 mm half-step), chord step 20 mm. Manufacturing: a single sheet is at most 400 mm; not a search limit, shaded in the atlas.
